scope: Independent local code, synthetic ASGI tests, cached payload roundtrip, and non-applying patch check. This is not integration, live traffic, performance, or deployment approval.

coverage: Eligible gzip and identity representations preserve Vary and policy headers
Explicit gzip q=0 overrides wildcard and duplicate positive acceptance
Small, streaming, SSE, no-transform, ETag and already encoded responses are excluded
Raw ASGI compressed bytes decompress exactly and compressed Content-Length is correct
All Cache-Control and Vary header fields, including wildcard Vary, are respected
Response start precedes extensions; trailer-declared responses are excluded
SSE response start is forwarded before a deliberately delayed first event

patch_check.baseline: Exact locally saved live-G server hash, corroborated against local canary-promotion-pass.json and live-verify.json; no remote verification in this audit.
patch_check.not_baseline: Dirty backend/server.py SHA256 e47b8d27bc3d8dacf5018a9b8bcd131551d6760c1b2a4708611252463c058b2a was inspected but is not the final insertion-patch base.

resolved_findings: Previously ignored later Cache-Control fields now prevent compression when any field specifies no-transform.
Previously overwritten duplicate Vary fields are preserved; Accept-Encoding is appended only when needed.
Held response start is flushed before ASGI representation extensions; trailer-declared responses pass through.
Known-ineligible SSE and non-JSON response starts no longer wait for the first body event.
The earlier nested-directory Git check skipped its target. The corrected contextual patch was independently checked from repository root against the actual saved live-G target without a skip.
middleware_order: Proposed registration immediately after FastAPI construction is inner to subsequently registered CORS and request-policy middleware. Existing outer authentication, security, cookie and cache policies remain outside compression. No server integration was performed.
limitations: Potentially eligible JSON headers wait for the first body frame to distinguish single-body from streamed JSON. Later streamed frames are not collected or compressed.
Compression reduces transferred bytes, not lookup cost or browser rendering workload.
Deployment must independently verify the actual target source, middleware stack and hosted behavior.
